intro.title: Build typed dependency container
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed dependency container in TypeScript, a tool for managing and injecting service instances in an application. You'll learn the core concept of dependency injection, which helps organize code by decoupling classes from their dependencies. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's interfaces, generics, and classes to ensure type safety. By the end, you'll have a functional container that can register and resolve services with full type checking.
intro.usecase: Typed dependency containers are essential in large-scale applications like e-commerce dashboards or enterprise admin panels, where managing dozens of services—such as user authentication, payment gateways, and data analytics—must be type-safe and maintainable. For example, in a dashboard that displays real-time sales data, filters, and interactive charts, a typed container ensures that each UI component receives correctly structured API clients and state managers without runtime errors. This pattern allows developers to swap implementations (like mocking a service during testing) while keeping the application's architecture clean and predictable, directly improving developer productivity and reducing bugs in complex product interfaces.
